Hey Meranda\!



Thank you for raising this. I’m sorry to hear Surgo agents are struggling, could you please elaborate if you’re seeing these issues with Majorel or IN agents as well? How have you detected those gaps, has this come up from ESC deep-dives or some other source we could take a look at?



Looking at the issues raised, this is all very closely connected to processes in KB that should be explained well enough as they are (e.g. [Eater requests their data|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360015271939--Eater-requests-their-data] KB article for your latest point). Quite frankly, I’m very against creating a “detailed guide” for the following questions mainly because that’s already present in KB. Below I’m linking the relevant articles and/or explanations to what you can do to ensure agents have the up-to-date info or what kind of training we already have. 




*What to do if providers say they cannot sign in, even after giving them the logins.* Do you have any examples? There’s an article [here|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008827559--Provider-can-t-log-in], 
*What can we change and not change on the provider's profile* Very much dependent on local work division between OPS/CS. I suppose more knowledge of provider portal and menu editor might be needed so that agents know what providers can do themselves (we do have a training in the [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:1155]).
*How to change their email - should we also change them on the ops sheet?* Again, very local specific, there’s no global process for this as local Partner OPS might have their own sheet which isn’t available everywhere. What you can do in case you want this in any way specified is raise a request to the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620] and have this added in KB if justified.
*If an internal note is sent to us from JIRA, do we reply back with the internal note?* This will not be an issue much longer as Jira won’t be available in Beehive, although we did have proper training on Jira Escalations, now also available from the [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:632])
*How to send them statements/invoices, and what procedures to take* multiple articles available in KB ([Provider earnings|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360002187659-Provider-earnings-payments])
*What discounts we can and can not escalate,* *What menu changes we can and not escalate* Again, very local specific, although some articles are available (e.g. [this one|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403350463634--Provider-wants-to-add-a-promo]), there is already some country-specific info, so you can raise a request to the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620] and have this added in KB if needed.
*If a provider contacts us saying they are struggling to make changes on their menu using the menu editor, and they have gone through the menu editor, and are still struggling, can we then escalate this to Jira? Or how do we solve it?* This is rather up to local partner OPS, ideally, though I would say share the relevant FAQ articles to help them make those changes. 
*When working on a beehive and we need to contact either provider or courier, are there any procedures we need to follow on ZD(such as inserting a comment with the beehive link, etc)* Not sure I understand this one, on Beehive you’ll see actors of the order and will be able to contact them through the ticket. 
*When a provider requests changes in their prices, for certain items, but also requests a discount (20% off) at the same time for different items, when it comes to selecting an ATI, will we select  "I have a question about menu management" or " I have an issue with a campaign or bonus"* We don’t have ATIs anymore, but when it comes to issues - on Beehive you could select both if relevant (like here), in Zendesk now you can only opt for one of them, so go for the one that seems more important. Careful tho, don’t look too much into root causes, just what’s reported.
*Menu editor/JIRA escalations* Can be very local-specific, but we do have the course in [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:632]


*How to compensate drivers that drive extra km* couriers? In which situations? When address is changed, earnings should be adjusted. If you’re missing guidelines for some other cases or specific steps, please raise this with the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620]
*In what situations should we block drivers* please see [courier blocking guidelines|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/5525565903122--Courier-blocking-guidelines] :)
*What to do in situations when courier complain about eaters behavior* please see [article|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360019933919--Eater-behaviour-complaint]
*When can we unblock couriers?* please see [courier blocking guidelines|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/5525565903122--Courier-blocking-guidelines] :)
*What to do if they are experiencing technical problems with the app?* depending on which issues, some articles from the [Courier account|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360002187699-Courier-account] category cover that, if not, we have [courier tech issues|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360005455799-Courier-tech-issues] category
*How to send invoices/statements* please see [Courier invoice and report info|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360011555179--Courier-invoice-and-report-info] or [Courier has an invoice issue|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4404300420754--Courier-has-an-invoice-issue]
*What statements can we send or not send* as above, explanations are in the articles
*Can we update banking details?* please see [Courier wants to update banking details|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008752840--Courier-wants-to-update-banking-details]

Hey Meranda\!



Thank you for raising this. I’m sorry to hear Surgo agents are struggling, could you please elaborate if you’re seeing these issues with Majorel or IN agents as well? How have you detected those gaps, has this come up from ESC deep-dives or some other source we could take a look at?



Looking at the issues raised, this is all very closely connected to processes in KB that should be explained well enough as they are (e.g. [Eater requests their data|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360015271939--Eater-requests-their-data] KB article for your latest point). Quite frankly, I’m very against creating a “detailed guide” for the following questions mainly because that’s already present in KB. Below I’m linking the relevant articles and/or explanations to what you can do to ensure agents have the up-to-date info or what kind of training we already have. 


*What to do if providers say they cannot sign in, even after giving them the logins.* Do you have any examples? There’s an article [here|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008827559--Provider-can-t-log-in], 
*What can we change and not change on the provider's profile* Very much dependent on local work division between OPS/CS. I suppose more knowledge of provider portal and menu editor might be needed so that agents know what providers can do themselves (we do have a training in the [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:1155]).
*How to change their email - should we also change them on the ops sheet?* Again, very local specific, there’s no global process for this as local Partner OPS might have their own sheet which isn’t available everywhere. What you can do in case you want this in any way specified is raise a request to the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620] and have this added in KB if justified.
*If an internal note is sent to us from JIRA, do we reply back with the internal note?* This will not be an issue much longer as Jira won’t be available in Beehive, although we did have proper training on Jira Escalations, now also available from the [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:632])
*How to send them statements/invoices, and what procedures to take* multiple articles available in KB ([Provider earnings|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360002187659-Provider-earnings-payments])
*What discounts we can and can not escalate,* *What menu changes we can and not escalate* Again, very local specific, although some articles are available (e.g. [this one|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4403350463634--Provider-wants-to-add-a-promo]), there is already some country-specific info, so you can raise a request to the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620] and have this added in KB if needed.
*If a provider contacts us saying they are struggling to make changes on their menu using the menu editor, and they have gone through the menu editor, and are still struggling, can we then escalate this to Jira? Or how do we solve it?* This is rather up to local partner OPS, ideally, though I would say share the relevant FAQ articles to help them make those changes. 
*When working on a beehive and we need to contact either provider or courier, are there any procedures we need to follow on ZD(such as inserting a comment with the beehive link, etc)* Not sure I understand this one, on Beehive you’ll see actors of the order and will be able to contact them through the ticket. 
*When a provider requests changes in their prices, for certain items, but also requests a discount (20% off) at the same time for different items, when it comes to selecting an ATI, will we select  "I have a question about menu management" or " I have an issue with a campaign or bonus"* We don’t have ATIs anymore, but when it comes to issues - on Beehive you could select both if relevant (like [here|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4405241090322--Adding-case-issues]), in Zendesk now you can only opt for one of them, so go for the one that seems more important. Careful tho, don’t look too much into root causes, just what’s reported.
*Menu editor/JIRA escalations* Can be very local-specific, but we do have the course in [course catalog|https://boltcs.talentlms.com/catalog/info/id:632]


*How to compensate drivers that drive extra km* couriers? In which situations? When address is changed, earnings should be adjusted. If you’re missing guidelines for some other cases or specific steps, please raise this with the [Content Team|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/group/127/create/620]
*In what situations should we block drivers* please see [courier blocking guidelines|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/5525565903122--Courier-blocking-guidelines] :)
*What to do in situations when courier complain about eaters behavior* please see [article|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360019933919--Eater-behaviour-complaint]
*When can we unblock couriers?* please see [courier blocking guidelines|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/5525565903122--Courier-blocking-guidelines] :)
*What to do if they are experiencing technical problems with the app?* depending on which issues, some articles from the [Courier account|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360002187699-Courier-account] category cover that, if not, we have [courier tech issues|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/sections/360005455799-Courier-tech-issues] category
*How to send invoices/statements* please see [Courier invoice and report info|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360011555179--Courier-invoice-and-report-info] or [Courier has an invoice issue|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4404300420754--Courier-has-an-invoice-issue]
*What statements can we send or not send* as above, explanations are in the articles
*Can we update banking details?* please see [Courier wants to update banking details|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360008752840--Courier-wants-to-update-banking-details]

So the plan is taking shape as follows:

* {{delivery-provider-app}} to keep its own copy of {{order_flow_settings}} and {{order_type}} per provider;
* {{delivery-provider-app}} to listen to {{provider-metadata}} events;
* for a given event, check local copy of {{order_flow_settings}} and compare against payload - if restart should be applied (values have changed), trigger restart.

Pitfall: initializing the values in {{delivery-provider-app}} (or _not_ initializing them and treating empty local value as restart trigger).

Pitfall: we only need to keep local copies of this data to determine if restart is needed - seems wasteful.

In an ideal version we would receive before/after values or diffs in these events, but this is what we have to work with for now.

Hiring:

h3. *Task 1: Resume/CV Screening:*

*Example responses:*

# _I would not proceed with an interview for this candidate. There is no information about the individual on their resume. No education or employment history, and even their objective is rather vague. The candidate also stated that his or her first preference is a project management role. But the application is for a CS role. Meaning that the resume may not have been adjusted or updated before submission._
# _I would definitely arrange an interview with this candidate. They seem to have very good vocabulary and written English which is a huge plus for a customer support role. The candidate is bilingual and very involved in different activities and projects. Although their background is more related to marketing and research, from the resume I would say they are a good communicator. However, with such vast experience, I would be curious why this candidate would be applying for a customer support role._
# _I would not arrange an interview with this candidate. The candidate does not have sufficient written communication skills for the role (grammatical errors). Their responses are informal with the use of slang, answers are very short and vague. They have not put much effort into the task and there are no examples or explanations to back up their answers. The last response from the candidate is completely unrelated to the question._

h3. *Task 2: Application question responses:*

*Example responses (only 1 answer is required but these are some examples):*

*Question 1:*

* What specifically attracted you to Bolt?
* What experience/s have you had with our company/brand?

*Question 2:*

* *_Give me an example of a time you gave a customer great service._* _(_reason: Great candidates should have specific stories of interactions they’ve had with customers. It demonstrates that they really do empathize with the individuals they’re serving and understand the value of great service._)_
* *_What makes for great customer support?_* (reason: This question should give you a sense of how the candidate views their role. A great answer won’t just involve solving a problem or answering a question, but ensuring that the customer had as positive an interaction as possible.)
* *What do you enjoy about customer support/service?* (reason: It’s important for customer support agents to be empathetic and people-oriented. Good answers might include “I like talking to people and finding out about their lives” or “I love the feeling of helping somebody solve a problem they’re having.”)

*Question 3:*

* Could you elaborate a little more on that, what do you enjoy about learning?
* Could you provide me with examples of your self-development? Why did you pursue this?
* What is one thing that you recently learnt?

*Question 4:*

* You would not want to do anything for yourself with some of the money?
* Would you be happy to continue working and earning a living?
* Why would you give all the money to charity?

*Question 5:*

* Why is customer support experience important?
* What makes customer support/service great?
* How can you ensure a great customer support process?
* What are some ways we can eliminate bad customer support?

h3. *Task 3: Candidate questions during interviews:*

*Example response:*

# _The job does indeed involve supporting our users over the phone as well as through e-mail and in-app messaging. As this is a customer support role, the users reach out to us with a problem or to report an unpleasant experience so there may be times that you need to handle a dissatisfied customer._ 
# _The role consists of 3 different shifts which includes nights and weekends. This is allocated between the team evenly through a schedule and it would mean working a maximum of 6 weekend shifts per month._ 
# _Yes\! Bolt has a variety of events that are arranged by the company for all employees to attend, and we often arrange events with our team to get to know one another and spend quality time together._ 
# _We have offices in Tartu and Tallinn where it is possible for you to work from and there is an option to work remotely. However, there may be instances where we will meet at the office as team on days we have team meetings scheduled._
# _Flexi hours refers mostly to different start times for early shifts. For example, we have 3 start times: 7:00am -15:30pm, 8:00am - 16:30pm and 9:00am - 17:30pm. However, late or night shifts have set start times. Remote working has become more popular nowadays, and the option is always there but we don't recommend that you work from home 100% of the time as we'd still like to see you face to face and working from the office will help you to get to know the team._ 

h3. *Task 4: Rejections, feedback and in-interview tactics*

# *_Definitely give the compliment first_*_. Knowing you have done something right may make the negative feedback more acceptable. Giving the bad news first can make the compliment seem patronizing or condescending._
# _I think we can explain that they were on the right track when it comes to their answers, however, the responses were not quite what we were looking for. We can also say that it did not appear as they were passionate about the role and we couldn't sense a positive working attitude._ 
# _This would depend if you are really keen on meeting the candidate. However, should they not respond to the invite after a few days, a rejection email can be sent with a reason._
# _Having done interviews recently, I found that two candidates with educational backgrounds in data sciences and analyzing with no experience in the customer support field. During the interview, it was visible that they are not suitable for a customer support role and we did not proceed further with their interviews. We are not looking for candidates to join the team just because it is an entry-level job and they wish to get into the company somehow with no interest in the role they've applied for._ 
# _There should be some ice-breakers at the beginning of the interview to take pressure off the candidate and make sure they're comfortable with you. I would then begin with asking easier questions as I would like to give them a fair chance and not throw them off in any way. This way the candidate has time to adjust and when we move onto the more serious questions, they are more prepared._ 
# _I think the best way to get the candidate to open up, is to ask them to give (real-life) examples of situations they have been in to back up their answer. This way they are talking about their personal experiences which helps to get to know them better and gives me, as the interviewer, a better understanding of the explanation they're trying to give._ 
# _I don't think it is wise to end the interview too soon, as the candidate may feel as though we are not even giving them a fair chance (in may result in bad press). I would still ask the necessary questions to be able to give some feedback on the scorecard afterward. However, I would not ask the candidate for further elaboration on their answer or dig deeper into their responses._ 
# _Why have you decided to apply for a position at Bolt and where do you see yourself in a year? My preferred answer would be, that the candidate is interested in what we have to offer as a company, the benefits and working environment, teams, etc. Also, I would hope that they are interested in developing professionally within Bolt and see themselves still working here in a year._ 
# _Usually the second round interview is to get to know the candidate more and if they would be a good fit for the team. The job specific interview questions are covered in the first round and the second round is a good opportunity to get a difference in opinion from other interviewers. The downside of conducting an interview with the STL and TL, is that the TL maybe feels as though they have to agree with their manager regarding the overall decision. However, the STL is not as directly involved in the day-to-day tasks of the team and mostly concentrates on the bigger picture. So, certain aspects that were identified in the candidate during the first round, will not be visible in the second round to the STL and why they would be a good fit for the team._

* *Mechanism of this Lease Agreement:* 

It is a promissory agreement that contains all the clauses for the future definitive lease agreement.

The Use License is an essential document for signing the Lease Agreement. For this reason, this is a promissory agreement that will become a definitive lease agreement when the User License is issued. Until the issuance of this Use License, BOLT may start using the Premises. When the Use License is issued, the definitive agreement is signed and the start date is reported as June 1st.

When the Use License is issued, the definitive lease agreement will be signed, which is this promissory agreement, removing the clauses of the promise (which are intended to be in force until the definitive lease).

As a rule, this situation in Portugal has no associated risk. This risk will always be the responsibility of the Landlord (final part of paragraph 8 of Clause 17)..

DLA confirmed there's no need to add a right for us to terminate the contract (promising and definitive) if the landlord doesn't obtain the building license by the end of July 2022, because issuing the Use License could take some time.

* *Right for the landlord to terminate the contract / kick us out of the warehouse:*

The Landlord can only terminate the lease if BOLT has defaulted, in particular due to the payment of rents. The term of the agreement is 5 years, so the Landlord can only terminate it towards the end of the term.

[https://wellarchitectedlabs.com/cost/200_labs/200_4_cost_and_usage_analysis/3_cur_analysis/|https://wellarchitectedlabs.com/cost/200_labs/200_4_cost_and_usage_analysis/3_cur_analysis/] 

In order to do this, we should enable Cost & Usage Report daily forwarding to a S3 bucket which could be queried by Athena.

[https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/billing/home?region=us-east-1#/reports|https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/billing/home?region=us-east-1#/reports]

It’s possible to get info for:

*Top Costs*:

* Top Costs by AccountID
* Top Costs by Product
* Top Costs by Line Item Description
* Top EC2 Costs
* Top EC2 OnDemand Costs

*Cost Allocation*:

* Top Costs by line item description and CostCenter Tag
* Top costs by line item description, without a CostCenter Tag

*Savings Plans, Reserved Instance, On Demand and Spot Usage:*

* *Who used Savings Plan* Identify which usage was covered by a savings plan.
* *Unused Savings Plan* For each savings plan, look at the total commitment and total usage each month.
* *Who used Reserved Instances* Identify which accounts used the available RIs, and what they would have paid with public pricing. Ideal for chargeback within an organization.
* *Specific Instance family usage* Observe how much is being spent on each different family (usage type) and how much is covered by Reserved instances.
* *Costs By running type* Divide the cost by usage (hrs), and see how much is being spent per hour on each of the usage types. Compare *BoxUsage* (On Demand), to *HeavyUsage* (Reserved instance), to *SpotUsage* (Spot).
* *Show unused Reserved Instances* This will show how much of your reserved instances are not being used, and sorts it via cost of unused portion (recurring fee).

• fee for 1 minute - PLN 0.30

Fist of all, my sincere apologies for the slow reply 🙏  as you may know I attended the Legal Summit last week and now I am trying to catch up on everything.

Regarding clause 6.2, we do not want to be exposed to unlimited liability, therefore, *we cannot accept unlimited liability (as suggested by the client) but we can accept liability greater than 3 months (which is the maximum liability in the original wording).*

This means that we are willing to reword clause 6.2 to increase the liability cap and hence it can be worded as follows:

* replacing the original wording with the following: _‘The liability of Bolt in connection with any loss or damage that Customer may incur as a result of using Bolt Business shall be equal to \[… euros]_; or

Hm, for this need to take a look how it works 🙂 
Current EC2: 
We have etcd cluster with 5 nodes (etcd-1,etcd-2…etcd-5). 
To be able to send requests to all nodes of etcd we use etcd-gateway on each instance which knows via configuration parameters about each etcd host. So it listen localhost:2379 and proxy request from this address to on of etcd node which are defined in configuration of etcd-gateway. So that also means, if we will scale number of etcd-nodes, we also need to upgrade configuration of etcd-gateway across all instances. 

Kubernetes: 
We have etcd-cluster in dedicated namespace, and it has [kubernetes service|https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/service/] object with url: etcd-server.etcd, which automatically discovery each pod of etcd cluster, and proxy all connections from this url to etcd nodes. So it do the same thing what etcd-gateway, but from the box. 

So that is why etcd-gateway in kubernetes architecture is extra component. 

Plus etcd-gateway also able to work now, because it share the host via “host network mode“, but in future we need to rid off from this.

So deployment + service is a standard pair for providing communication between containers. 
How it works: 

For example, we have deployment object for service A:

{noformat}Deployment:
  Label:
    name: ServiceA
  Replicas: 10
  Container:
    Image: docker.registry.io/serviceA
  Ports: 8080{noformat}

And for service B: 

{noformat}Deployment:
  Label:
    name: serviceB
  Replicas: 5
  Container:
    Image: docker.registry.io/serviceB
  Ports: 8080{noformat}

After that we will get 10 replicas for serviceA and 5 replicas of serviceB. 

If we want to sent request from serviceB to serviceA, we need to create kubernetes service which will be discover all replicas of one of service and send request to one if them. 

{noformat}Service: 
  name: serviceA-special-long
  Selector: 
    name: serviceA
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8080{noformat}

So, now if I will exec in one of replica of service B, I’m able to make 

{noformat}curl serviceA-special-long
200 - respond replica 1 
curl serviceA-special-long
200 - respond replica 2 {noformat}

And so on. 

About this task: 
We already have and deployment and service deployed by core-builder. But the issue is that we use hostPort in kubernetes. 
That means, that we bind some port on host where pod is deployed. In case of kubernetes - it’s orchestrator and from deployment perspective it’s abstracted from ec2 instances. So for example we may have 3 ec2 instances for running workload in kubernetes, and want to scale some service to 12 replicas, it will not work, because ports will be bind to instance and it will not allow to allocated additional replicas on these 3 hosts. 

Ideally, in terms of “kubernetes abstractions” all nodejs services may listen by default port 80, we just need to create service for each deployment (it’s a normal practice) which will be route the traffic to all replicas of nodejs-services and never think about which ports are free.

For driver faults etc driver has obligatory insurance in place. Do check out [the “Liability” section in the FAQ|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/2923692552/FAQ.+Legal.+Team+Account+Ride+Booker] for this purpose.

So what is this 6.2 for? 

(Off record) it has never(\!) been applied so far over the years, and I hope it hardly ever will be. Theoretically it covers cases where Bolt Business (b2b software) fails so bad that it causes damage to Customer. So mainly undirect damages, loss of profits. Please also note 6.1 (Bolt Business and Services are provided “as is”) so that should further cover our back. This is the reason we are so generous in terms of limiting our liability for this - to remove any friction from onboarding Customers. Going forward as we grow we’ll take more and more the direction of limiting even this theoretical liability. And changing this “equal to” to “limited to” is the first step.

Is 6.2 smoke and mirrors? Yes, you can say that. And tbh, let’s keep it that way. So why not compromise on smth like: _“The liability of Bolt in connection with any loss or damage that Customer may incur as a result of using Bolt Business shall be limited to the actual and substantiated direct damages Customer has suffered but will in all cases be limited to the actual amount received by Bolt from the Customer under the Agreement in \[12] months preceding the date on which the claim arose.”_

*There are two main issues* I observed after evaluating all change requests.

1️⃣  *Users often report missing car keys, even though the car keys are there* (left in a strange place by the previous user, such as behind or under the seat, between the seat and the cup holder, etc.)

We can address this by making the first step in the process to ask the user to check the car carefully, as the keys are often in the car, just not in a clear place. This is actually suggested in the self-help article I can’t find the car keys. However, not all users may check it before contacting support, and support also doesn’t confirm if the user has indeed checked the whole car.

2️⃣ *Users who have taken and are not returning the car keys*

✔️ The current process already covers the steps to inform the user with the car keys that they have 30 min to return them back to us, otherwise fines according to our List of Penalties and Additional Fees will apply. Henriko mentioned that these steps (added to the process on Feb 10) are making the users return the keys faster (although I don’t have specific data to share). Therefore we can focus on fines and dealing with repeat offenders.

3️⃣ *The current process doesn’t include any instructions for repeat offenders* (users who may have taken the car keys multiple times already)

To address this, we can make the following changes to the current process:

* Have agents add a comment both on the order page, as well as the user’s profile page in Admin (currently, comments are left on the order page only)
* Implement a blocking logic based on the number of comments already on the user’s profile page - we can follow the blocking standards for Regular high priority events.
** One question is - do we want to hard-block the user at the 4th report, or give them an opportunity to rethink their behaviour and change it once the block time passes? (we will also use this logic for the Speeding reports process update, published later this week).

Hey [~accountid:619df38fc75da8007295630e]\!

You can find the longer privacy analysis on the feature [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hCBfqegns-wY4ybOaC13C5BEyD1XVD8DFb9tsIE40Dw/edit]. But I will add here the recap of our advice to facilitate this: 

# *Enabling the feature:*
Audio recording is started when one of the parties initiates the recording under the safety features (i.e. pushes the button to record my ride). 
# *Transparency and notification requirements:* 
- Microphone icon with small notice that audio on your ride could be recorded when ride is ordered/accepted by the driver (so that riders and drivers are notified before each ride). Or a microphone icon which leads to FAQ article about explaining the feature;
- The other party on the trip is notified when audio recording for the trip ongoing is initiated;
- Privacy notices (both passenger and drivers) shall include information about the data processing, purposes which Bolt uses the recordings, who it will be disclosed to etc. → let's align prior to launching for us to make necessary updates. 
# *Retention:*
- 24hr if safety case is not initiated (deleted after that). 
- If incident is reported, retention time should be aligned with storing CS tickets in general (24 months at the moment) in order to investigate the incident and resolve any disputes necessary. 
# *Storage:*
- Bolt will not have access to recordings unless the safety case is initiated. 
- Storing in User’s device and providing access to Bolt. Here we need the user to allow us access this/upload to our servers when safety case is initiated. This can be done by asking user to allow/enable Bolt to access Files/Media in their settings. 

On launching in Nigeria - Nigeria is a different market where we need user’s consent. Therefore before launching this feature there, we would need advice from local counsel how to facilitate this in compliance with Nigerian Data Protection Regulation. Therefore I suggest starting testing first in South Africa.

The hardcoded port requirement per service instance was historically there, I don’t think it is a hard requirement, if routing layer, monitoring layer and logging layer can handle dynamic allocation.

Currently our logger script resolves some log metadata based on hostname:port combination.

In live-logs* machines, there is /etc/discovery-list.txt file that is updated every 5 minutes. The data for is is collected from etcd.

It looks like this:

{noformat}root@live-logs-1:~# head /etc/discovery-list.txt -n 5
827 ttl	n37:5022	ride-history-admin	rides	live-ridearchive
641 ttl	n38:5022	ride-history-admin	rides	live-ridearchive
746 ttl	n39:5022	ride-history-admin	rides	live-ridearchive
630 ttl	live-gb-n3:8464	britain-order-polling	rides	live-orderpolling-britain
630 ttl	live-gb-n3:8566	britain-order-polling	rides	live-orderpolling-britain{noformat}


It is used by logger script, this data is used to resolve service name, owner team and package in nodejs logs.

But because of this architecture with cron scripts being not realtime, allocating ports dynamically at every deployment would break resolving these fields, also possibly produce wrong values if same port is reused by different service.

Also, I think there is a similar thing for NodeJS service metrics/dashboards on monitor.internal (has to be double checked).

IMO the hardcoded ports is a should not be a requirement, but these logging and monitoring flows would have to be improved to allow fully dynamic ports.

After spending long time reading through materials, laws, and orders, I found no specific requirements that need to be present before we can conclude distance selling of pastries. This can be summarised as follows:

In the case of *non-prepacked foods* offered for sale by means of distance communications, the food business operator is required to provide only *allergen information* in accordance with the particulars under Article 44 of the Regulation, unless national measures require the provision of all or some of the particulars referred to in Articles 9 and 10 of the Regulation. The allergen information and any other particulars required by national law shall be provided *before the purchase is concluded* by either appearing on the material supporting the distance selling (e.g. webpage or catalogue) or through other appropriate means clearly identified by the food business operator without any supplementary costs for the final consumer. In addition, *at the moment of delivery*, the responsible food business operator is required to make available the allergen information and any other particulars required by national law (Art. 14, par. 2).

She also explained that the jurisprudence in France is very clear: any instant messaging / chats offered by the employer has a professional purpose and therefore can be accessed by the employers, as long as this is justified and proportionate to the end goal. These messages are not meant to be personal, the employer is meant to be able to access them as long as it is obvious that the messaging/chat has a professional purpose. Which we think is the case for Slack messages.

*In her view, the fact for us to access Slack messages from employees who have been committing fraud to gather evidence for disciplinary procedures is legitimate and proportionate.* 

The only exception could be for messages that are clearly marked as ‘Personal and Confidential’ but even then the jurisprudence is not that clear.

Hi\! 

I am confident that adding an issue type called _Active delivery issue_ would certainly not help us identify any root causes in a better way than what we have today. 

_Active delivery issue_ is an umbrella term, which would cover every single issue type during an active order (ranging from GPS issues to order delays to missing items). That would mean that, instead of the 40-50 issue types we have per user type, we would have only one called _Active delivery issue._ Each time that we’d want to find out what the problem is - we would have to deep-dive into it, because we would only know that the problem is about an active delivery. The system we have today is meant to cover these specific scenarios and thus already provide a much clearer understanding of what the issue was without looking much into it. 

Also, whether or not an issue is about an active order doesn’t often change the problem. If an Eater contacts about missing items, the problem will be the same regardless of when they contact us. 

I just can’t see how slicing our reporting by active vs non-active orders would make any difference whatsoever. To find root causes, we need to understand the reasons why users contact us, not when they contact us.

Robert

Hello\! 

This is what the driver lifecycle pretty much looks like: 

# Driver lead will send their documents to Bolt. 
# Bolt will review driver documents, if everything seems to be in order, the driver will be invited to driver hub for onboarding. 
# At the onboarding appointment hub agent will upload the driver’s documents to the driver profile and activate the driver. 
# The driver leaves driver hub with an activated profile and starts booking trips. 
# At a certain point of the driver lifecycle, some documents expire (e.g. many drivers have weekly or monthly insurance certificates, meaning that they need to reupload their renewed documents every week or month).
# When driver documents expire they get automatic comms from the app to reupload the expired doc. This is where the problem arises - the driver does not know how to upload new documents, the driver gives up, stays idle (or churns) and uses competitors' apps instead. 
_Sometimes the driver contacts CS via Zendesk to know which document he needs to upload but from CS he’s getting advice on material matters (e.g. what documents need uploading, what the quality of the picture should be etc) but he doesn’t get any instructions on how to actually use the app to upload the docs._ 

To avoid drivers churning, we’d like to have a self-help article with screenshots on how to upload the documents. The self-help article can be integrated into the automatic comms that are sent out when documents expire + CS agents can link the article when drivers reach out to them.

Again, I’m happy to put together a mock-up of the article to show you guys what contents we need from the article. And you can take the mock-up, polish it off, cross the t’s and dot the i’s etc. 



Let me know, if there are any other details I can provide you guys with :)

*Discussion with Akbar Gulaliyev (Partner Operations Specialist, AZ)*

Food provider uses gross settlement because it is required by AZ tax regulations. Provider pay the VAT and net commission to two separate bank accounts. 

So in summary

* Bolt asking for payment once per month
* For restaurants not paying >1 month, Bolt suspends payout to the provider
** Case: Shazeli group accrued ~60k EUR debt and refused to pay Bolt back. Then, Bolt stopped the payout to the company. Later the company pay off their debt only for 1 provider, thus restarting the payout for that 1 provider while still suspend payout for other providers.
** Case: McD’s debt is big because of their transaction volume. Usually they pay off their debt each month.
* AZ local team tracking the debt manually with Google sheet, because
** the Look doesn't show actual data, because for providers with > 1 branch during first month with Bolt send the money as a sum for all branches (not for individual branch) without a reference number (hence, the payment is not automatically matched).
*** Debt is monitored on company-level (1 company may own >1 vendor such as Shazeli group), and calculated manually by local ops
** Debt data is collected manually per VOEN (company reg code) on restaurant basis (not individual branch basis)
** AZ local team and partner payment specialist were educating providers and majority of them paying in the correct way, with reference number.



*Solutions in place*

# Stop payout for providers with >1 month unpaid commission

Hi all,

I think this request may have gone off track. The regulatory team should have reviewed only if the introduction of the T&Cs would have any impact to our existing licenses - i.e. whether we need to notify any regulatory authority about introducing these T&Cs, whether it would be better to delete the part about TopUps so as to avoid regulatory attention and the like.

+If there are no ride hailing or rentals licenses in Croatia, then the regulatory team should not do anything in connection with the roll-out of these T&Cs at the moment.+

For all issues with Bolt Balance, in general, the legal team is handling these. A longer overview of these issues is provided below.

*INTRODUCTION*

For everyone to be aligned, Bolt Balance without the TopUp function is currently available in almost all of these jurisdictions. For some reason, it was launched in December 2021 without having properly consulted the legal or the regulatory teams. So, what we are currently doing is launching T&Cs for a feature, which is already out there.

The T&Cs describe the product as it is. We know that there are aspects to Bolt Balance and aspects to the way in which we currently handle refunds in general, which are not compliant with applicable law. And we need to address these. But we need to fix the product first and then follow up with T&Cs. The T&Cs describe the product as it is. Currently, it just makes sense to have T&Cs for a product which is already out there instead of not having any T&Cs to the product at all.

Below is an overview of some of the issues we face with or in connection with Bolt Balance.

*ISSUES*

*TopUps*

Without having analysed the local laws of all relevant jurisdictions, on the basis of EU legislation, the legal assessment is that +there is no significant risk of Bolt Balance being qualified as a payment instrument for e-money or as any other feature or functionality which would require that Bolt obtains a respective license as long as Bolt Balance does not have the TopUp function+. If Bolt Balance has the TopUp function, then there is a risk that Bolt Balance is qualified as a payment instrument for e-money and require that Bolt obtains a relevant license. More details about this are shared in this [memo|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M4H5QcaDhqDuRgRh69GQLy4ymC_PWj5j/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=103721628707869236107&rtpof=true&sd=true].

Because of the substantial legal risks to the TopUp function, rolling out the TopUp function has currently been halted in all jurisdictions and new jurisdictions are launched only after prior legal analysis and approval from our senior management. The approach which the commerce team is taking at the moment is that we launch the TopUp function in certain meaningful markets to test whether there is an actual business case to Bolt Balance and whether obtaining an electronic money institution license or partnering up with a licensed electronic money institution is worth the effort.

But again, the exercise which this spreadsheet is about, is about verifying whether there may be anything in our existing ride hailing licenses which may be an issue in rolling out these T&Cs. This exercise is not about verifying whether there may be an issue in our existing ride hailing licenses which may be an issue in rolling out the TopUp function.

*Refunds*

Consumer protection laws require that users be refunded in actual funds not Bolt Balance. This is not a question about the compliance of Bolt Balance. This is a question of how we handle refunds in general.

To my knowledge, as it stands today, we are technically unable to refund a card payment in part. So if a user got the burger but not the fries, then, without Bolt Balance, we have two options: (a) refund the user for the entire order; (b) not refund the user for anything. Currently, the position is that refunding the user to Bolt Balance is better than refunding the user for the entire order or not refunding the user for anything.

To my knowledge, before Bolt Balance, we did partial refunds in vouchers. So, nothing has really changed in that department – we were uncompliant in the way we handled refunds before and we are uncompliant with the way we handle refunds at the moment – with or without Bolt Balance. In order to get compliant, we need to develop the capability to do partial refunds of card payments.

If we want to be more aggressive on refunds, then what we could also do is that, by default, we would make refunds using Bolt Balance, but if a user insists on getting the refund in actual funds, then we would make the refund to the user’s card and reverse the addition of funds to Bolt Balance, or, alternatively, not make the refund to the user’s card, but allow the user to withdraw funds from Bolt Balance to the user’s card.  

However, as it currently stands, we are unable to do partial refunds to cards, we are unable to reverse refunds to Bolt Balance and we are unable to do withdrawals from Bolt Balance to the user’s card. So the only options we have are: (a) refund the user for the entire order; (b) not refund the user for anything; (c) refund the user using Bolt Balance. Currently, the preference is that we refund the user to Bolt Balance.

*Applicable Laws, Courts with Jurisdiction, Unilateral Transfers*

There are some aspects to not only the Bolt Balance T&Cs, but to all of our T&Cs, which are not compliant with applicable laws and which would need to be addressed.

Currently, the [Bolt Balance T&Cs|https://docs.google.com/document/d/18gZvAyaJNIn4c0vk-SZ78E0J1soDmue0/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=103721628707869236107&rtpof=true&sd=true] and the T&Cs for several other Bolt services stipulate that the T&Cs are subject to Estonian laws, that disputes are resolved in Estonian courts and that Bolt may transfer the contractual relationship on Bolt Balance to a third party without the user’s consent. In the EU, in accordance with laws implementing the [Unfair Contract Terms Directive|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A31993L0013], the [Consumer Rights Directive|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32011L0083], the [Omnibus Directive|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/2161/oj] and in accordance with the [Rome I Regulation|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=celex%3A32008R0593] and the [Brussels I Regulation|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=celex%3A32012R1215], all of these provisions are void an unenforceable vis-à-vis consumers.

In the Bolt Balance T&Cs, Section 13 has been added to mitigate the risk of sanctions being applied by consumer protection authorities due use of these void and unenforceable terms. Section 13 stipulates that mandatory consumer protection provisions of the country of the user’s habitual residence may override the provision on applicable law being Estonian and disputes being resolved in Estonian courts. However, most likely, this will not be deemed to render any T&Cs compliant with applicable consumer laws. And with the introduction of the Omnibus Directive, use of these terms may actually result in Bolt being issued penalties by consumer protection authorities.

 Therefore, we would need to amend all of our T&Cs to make sure that we comply with consumer protection laws. This is an exercise which requires a review of all of our T&Cs, not just Bolt Balance. And it makes sense to take a unified approach on this with respect to all of our T&Cs, not just Bolt Balance. This is something which has been raised with the heads of the product legal and field legal teams.

*CONCLUSION*

Drawing from the above, (i) to the extent it concerns TopUps, we are not launching that at the moment and this is not relevant for the exercise in this spreadsheet; (ii) to the extent it concerns refunds, we need to fix the product first and then follow up with T&Cs – right now, having T&Cs for a product, which is already out there is better than having no T&Cs; (iii) to the extent it concerns applicable laws, courts with jurisdiction, unilateral transfer of agreement, this is an issue with all of our T&Cs and needs to be addressed together with all of our T&Cs at a later stage.

{noformat}with rides as (

Select *
from (
  SELECT distinct o.user_id, 
  country.name as ride_country_name,
  city.name AS ride_city_name,
  o.created as first_ride,
  rank() over (partition by o.user_id order by o.created asc) as ride_num
  
  FROM public.company_order o
  JOIN public.company_order_try ot ON ot.city_id=o.city_id AND ot.order_id = o.id
  LEFT join admin_system_city city on city.id=o.city_id
  LEFT join admin_system_country country on country.code = o.country
  WHERE ot.state='finished' 
  )
where ride_num = 1
),

deliveries as (

Select *
  from (
  SELECT distinct d.master_user_id as user_id, 
  country.name as food_country_name , 
  city.name as food_city_name, 
  d.created as first_delivery,
  rank() over (partition by d.master_user_id order by d.created asc) as delivery_num
  
  FROM delivery.delivery_order_order d
  LEFT join admin_system_city city on city.id=d.city_id
  LEFT join admin_system_country country on country.code = d.country
  WHERE d.state = 'delivered'
  )
Where delivery_num = 1
)

from
rides FULL JOIN deliveries on rides.user_id = deliveries.user_id
group by 1

Hello Shanti,

The issues you are flagging relate to the quality of support. I’ll try to share with you some of my experience that will help the agents to reply to these tickets. It’s a long message, but I hope you’ll find it useful, please bear with me until the end 🙂 .

It’s nothing difficult with those cases, but it’s important to choose the right words when communicating with users and be confident of the investigation done in Admin. For a good quality investigation, please use the internal KB articles, which I’m sure you already know about, but they are always worth mentioning 🙂 :

* [ *User reports an unknown charge* |https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013746119--User-reports-an-unknown-charge]
* [*Pre-authorisation logic*|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360011785194--Pre-authorisation-logic]
* [*Pre-authorisation & authorisation*|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360005100694--Pre-authorisation-authorisation]
* [*Driver reports receiving requests outside the Radius*|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013052100--Driver-reports-receiving-requests-outside-the-Radius]



To come back to agents' struggles, It is true, we can’t improve the waiting time for a pre-authorization to return, because it does not depend on Bolt. The issue is related to the internal procedures and operations of the bank. What we can do instead, is to explain to the users that *from our side* the amount has been already released, and the waiting time depends on the bank. 

Be careful, do not use the word {color:#bf2600}*refunded*{color} for pre-authorizations, these *on-hold* transactions might never be shown in the transactions tab with a + in font, when they are released (e.g: +5 euros). Most often they simply disappear from the *Pending* tab. These details depend on the bank app settings. So to avoid all this confusion, it’s better to simply use the word {color:#36b37e}*released*{color}*.* The agents can also advise the user to check their *Pending* transactions in their bank app. 



Regarding the drivers' dissatisfaction on the radius, we can advise them how to set their radius at the minimum, 1km. The agents can also share the FAQ: [I receive orders outside my radius|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360010717420-I-receive-orders-outside-my-radius] which mentions that:

* they receive orders outside the selected radius *if* there are no other available drivers close to the rider’s pickup location
* the radius is measured *aerially*, and the actual driving distance may be longer than the radius distance.
* rejecting such orders *will not affect your activity score or your eligibility for specific bonus campaigns.*



The unsatisfaction of users increases when they receive robotic messages, without any personalization and when the issue it’s not explained. Encourage the agents to rather send a longer message that explains everything the user needs to know, ({color:#bf2600}*be careful, not internal info\!*{color}) rather than having a lot of back and forth messages. 

Explaining the why, using positive language and showing empathy are the soft skills the agents need to practice. 

To have a more clear answer to this soft skills part, you can share with the agents the *Reply Structure* presented below. Here is an example on how it works for pre-authorizations:

*Reply Structure:*

* {color:#ff5630}*Greeting*{color} 
** *Example:* Hello X, (always mention the name of the user)
* {color:#ff5630}*Thank the Customer for contacting (apologize if delayed)*{color}
** *Example:* Thank you for bringing this to our attention, I hope this message finds you well.
* {color:#ff5630}*Show empathy - acknowledge Customer’s feelings*{color} {color:#ff5630}*(if necessary)* {color}
** *_Example:_* “I understand it is upsetting to be charged for a ride that did not happen/be charged twice for the same ride, I would be upset too if I was in the same situation. It is a great thing that you brought this to my notice, I will look at this and assist you.”
* {color:#ff5630}*Acknowledge the issue(s) -* {color}{color:#ff5630}*_What the Customer wants/says?_*{color}
** *_Example:_* “After checking our data, I would like to inform you have not been charged for this order/ the amount charged for this order is “x”, which corresponds with the amount shown on the receipt.
* {color:#ff5630}*Investigate and explain -* {color}{color:#ff5630}*_What happened and why?_*{color}
** *_Example:_* The charge of “y” that you are seeing is a temporary pre-authorization hold coming from your bank to check your card’s validity and minimize any fraudulent use of your card and information.
This hold is released as soon as the ride is cancelled or completed. If not, it should be released within a few business days, depending on how fast your bank process is
* {color:#ff5630}*Solution -* {color}{color:#ff5630}*_What can I do?_*{color}
** *_Example:_* From our side, I can confirm that these funds have already been released back into your account.
* {color:#ff5630}*Education -* {color}{color:#ff5630}*_How can the Customer avoid the issue?_* {color}
** *_Example:_* If still, the funds aren't visible in your account, I would suggest you get in touch with your bank to confirm your balance status, but be rest assured the money will be reversed and will be visible in your account at the maximum by the promised time frame.
 
We hope that we were able to provide you with an appropriate explanation.You can also read the following article on the topic: [I was charged double for the same trip.|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-gb/articles/115002904873-I-Was-Charged-Double-for-the-Same-Trip]
* {color:#ff5630}*Encourage the Customer to contact again if needed -* {color}{color:#ff5630}*_Try to avoid the contact regarding the same issue by following the above points_* {color}
** *Example:* If there is anything else I can help you with, feel free to contact us.
* {color:#ff5630}*Sign off* {color}
** *Example*: Kind regards,    



If you have further questions, please feel free to reopen the ticket. 🙂

{code:sql}WITH stop_jitters AS (
  SELECT MIN(timestamp_ms) AS ts_start, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS ts_end, vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      SUM(igition_switch) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ignition_id
    FROM (
      SELECT *, 
        COALESCE((
          (ignition != LAG(ignition) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms)) OR
          (order_id != LAG(order_id) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms))
        )::integer, 1) AS igition_switch
      FROM (
        SELECT timestamp_ms, entity_id AS vehicle_id, order_id, 
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'is_ignition_on') AS ignition,
               lat, lng,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_pdop')::decimal AS gnss_pdop,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_hdop')::decimal AS gnss_hdop
        FROM ext_tracking_live.tracking_car_sharing_locations
        WHERE created_at_date>'2022-05-01' AND order_id!=0 AND JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_status')='fix'
          AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(lng,lat), ST_Point(24.745293, 59.437339)) < 15000 -- FILTER OUT FERRIES (hopefully), only 15km around Raekoja
          AND created_at_date='2022-05-14' AND order_id=3621305 -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
          -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-24' AND vehicle_id IN (1974,1254,777,1485,735,495,2013) -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
      )
    )
  )
  WHERE ignition='false'
  GROUP BY vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
)
SELECT vehicle_id, order_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, 
  MAX(distance_m) AS max_distance_m, 
  SUM(distinct_locations) AS distinct_locations,
    MIN(ts_start) AS ts_start, MAX(ts_end) AS ts_end
FROM (
  SELECT l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id, l.gnss_pdop, l.gnss_hdop,
    MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(l.lng, l.lat), ST_Point(r.lng, r.lat))) AS distance_m,
    SQRT(COUNT(1)) AS distinct_locations,
    MIN(l.ts_start) AS ts_start, MAX(l.ts_end) AS ts_end
  FROM stop_jitters AS l
  JOIN stop_jitters AS r ON (l.order_id = r.order_id AND l.ignition_id = r.ignition_id AND l.gnss_pdop = r.gnss_pdop AND l.gnss_hdop = r.gnss_hdop)
  GROUP BY l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id, l.gnss_pdop, l.gnss_hdop
  HAVING distance_m > 1
)
WHERE 1=1--gnss_pdop = 0 AND gnss_hdop = 0
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
ORDER BY max_distance_m DESC
LIMIT 100{code}

Hey there Guillaume. 

Just to clarify something first, despite the admin popup that says that blacklisted users are blocked from using cards, that information is wrong. Blacklist is just a fraud score and it’s not a blocker per se, the decision will depend on the whole fraud score. If the issue was just that the user is blacklisted, the solution would be identity verification, which removes the user from the blacklist. However, in this case, the verification won’t solve, as the user is triggering a rule related to business fraud that will continue to reject the user if they continue to use business as a payment method. 

In a few words, the solution here is to start Veriff identity verification + change the payment method. Once verified, the user can use the card as a payment method if they want to use our services.

In accordance with Croatian legislation the processing of personal data through video surveillance may be carried out only for the purpose necessary and justified for the protection of persons and property.

Video surveillance may include premises, parts of premises, external surface of a building, as well as internal space in public transport, and whose supervision is necessary in order to achieve the purpose,

The processing of personal data of employees through video surveillance systems may be carried out only if, the conditions determined by regulations governing occupational safety are met and if employees were duly notified in advance of such a measure before making a decision on setting up a video surveillance system.

Video surveillance of work premises must not include rooms for rest, personal hygiene and changing.

The processing manager or processor is obliged to indicate that the object or individual room in it and the outer surface of the object are under video surveillance, and the mark should be visible no later than when entering the perimeter of the recording.

The notification must contain all relevant information in accordance with the provisions of Article 13 of the General Data Protection Regulation, and in particular a simple and easy-to-understand image with the following information:

* that the space is under video surveillance
* data on the processing manager
* contact details through which the respondent can exercise his rights.

The right of access to personal data collected through video surveillance has the responsible person of the controller or executor of processing and / or a person authorized by him.

The processing manager and the processing executor must establish an automated record system for recording access to video surveillance recordings, which shall contain the time and place of access, as well as the designation of persons who accessed data collected through video surveillance.

Recordings obtained through video surveillance may be kept for a maximum of six months.

I totally understand this situation that you want to reported the fraudsters to the police, but we do have some more urgent matters, actual fraud losses that should be stopped ASAP, otherwise we will lose money, that is where we will put our attention. Plus in our experience these investigations really do not have the impact that everyone wishes for. They are very resource heavy, and could even end up damaging our Public Image if not doing carefully.

Regarding the accounts, sadly, we do not keep track of users accounts, in fact, not even the full card data is available to commerce team (or any other team).
Financial fraud (in the eyes of the police and/or payment providers is (as you said) X person uses Y persons card details without Y person authorising the transaction.
By the type of fraud I can 99% sure can tell you that those are not aiming to “cash-out” money from stolen cards.
The trip that you reported and the whole opportunity for the fraudster was due a bug on the migration for pre-authorization, the ride was XXX but we just pre-auth X amount, by the end of the ride the fraudster cancelled the card and we were not able to cash in the money. *We have fixed such bug* and the situation is now under control.

*Again, this is not financial fraud.* This is not what the police are really after, technically the rider is just owning us money for a trip, this is not different than someone not paying back an invoice from a service that already got.
 The owner of the card is very likely to be the same fraudsters that knew such card (probably a disposable card) will not have money.
Saying all that, I hope you understand that investigating and putting together the case and spending few hours for a fraud that already happened, we knew it happened and we took actions is not the best optimal usage of my time as a fraud analyst. If you wish to continue with this investigation I am happy to help, I will have this task on my personal bag-log but do not expect any replies anytime soon (specially since I am going on holidays in 3 days).

Hi Epp,

Apologies for the late response. Was traveling all of last week and only now catching up on my backlog. A quick explanation of the account / contract hierarchy in Adyen which I’m hoping will help clarify why the signing entity for the pricing is Bolt Technology and not Bolt Operations:

The highest hierarchy is something we call a Company Account. In our back-office it is named Taxify (an old Bolt name we are unable to change). The owner of this main account is Bolt Technology which is also the signing entity for the main Adyen Merchant Agreement.

Under the Company Account we have multiple Merchant Accounts - this is the next / second hierarchy level. These Merchant Accounts are owned by multiple Bolt entities depending on the entity who is actually processing payments in that Merchant Account.  So for example Merchant Account TaxifyGLOBAL is owned by Bolt Operations (and for that purpose we have an Affiliate Merchant Agreement with Bolt Operations) while that Merchant Account TaxifyEE is owned by Bolt Services EE Oܠ(and for that purpose we have an Affiliate Merchant Agreement with Bolt Services EE OÜ);

The transfer agreement you are pointing at was signed for the purpose of transferring the ownership of a few Merchant Accounts (listed in that signed document last page) from Bolt Technology to Bolt Operations. However - the main account / Company Account Taxify is still owned by Bolt Technology which is also the signing entity for the main Merchant Agreement.

We have a single place where we configure the Adyen pricing and it is in the Company Account Taxify. Therefore the pricing addendum is signed by the owner of the Company Account Taxify = Bolt Technology. Since that Company Account Taxify is the main account and the highest hierarchy - these pricing changes would apply to all Merchant Accounts and entities under it.

Hope this helps clarify and that we can now move forward to signatures.

*Business Monthly Invoices*

For business companies we are generating one invoice/statement per month. This is done on the 2nd each month & sent out the next day (i.e. 3rd each month). For March 2022 we’ve generated ~13k invoices from which 45% were sent a day or more late. The reason behind this is because we can send ~7200 invoices per day meaning it takes us roughly 3 days to deliver all the invoices for our business clients. 

From all of those >50% of the clients are using the credit card billing model meaning the invoice is just for the accounting purposes & no action is needed from the client. The remaining <50% of clients are using postpaid billing model meaning once they sign up we provide them with a credit limit which they can use for the month & after the period ends we charge them for the sum. For these companies seeing the actual invoice is important as then they know how to make the bank transfer. Now again the questions arise - should we even care about the invoices being sent late? 

From Looker we can see there are a some companies who are waiting to receive the email before making a payment to Bolt but the clients are more worried about the due date instead.

!Screenshot 2022-05-31 at 15.18.01.png|width=852,height=527!

From this it’s difficult to confirm if they’ve made a payment because they just received the email or because the due date is approaching. On average we see ~700 transfers per month within 3 days after they’ve received the email which equals to ~15% all payments done in the month. But are we possibly losing revenue because of this? The short answer is no, because the credit limit is set higher than the average sum of all rides taken within the month to take account the period between the invoice generation & the due date (usually it’s 15 days & we are sending out the email within 3 days). If the account is starting to hit their monthly limit we also send out reminders for them - an email if 75% of the limit is used & another one if 90% of the credit limit is used such that the business is aware they might hit their limit & the payment details can be found from the BP. Also if the business account hasn’t paid their invoice quickly we send out reminder emails 3 & 5 days later saying the account won’t be able to take any rides if the invoice isn’t cleared. If the account needs their invoice earlier it’s available on the Business Portal. 

Which comes to the CS tickets ~10% (~270 tickets ~675 EUR per month) of all are related to the question “Where’s my monthly invoice” & we do see a slight correlation if tickets submitted in the beginning of the month:

!Screenshot 2022-05-31 at 15.38.31.png|width=1112,height=536!

The communication improvements are being worked in [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BA-982|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/BA-982|smart-link] to make this clearer but in general business accounts will not get blocked because the invoice email is sent a day or two later than expected.

* Would there be regulatory risks relating to the delivery and/or the provision of the food in the name of Bolt Operations? It is worth mentioning that, from a VAT perspective, service provider is considered to be the entity issuing the invoice (i.e. Bolt Operations in this case). 
* How high do we consider the risk of the couriers being reclassified as employees, i.e. in a situation where Bolt is considered as the provider for food and delivery to the business customers? We do not believe that in Estonia that risk is too high, but perhaps it is worthwhile to also have a look from a regulatory/legal perspective?

* For self-billing (invoices generated by Bolt automatically on behalf of restaurants and couriers to Bolt) we would need to make sure that our T&C-s ask for written approval (for invoicing on behalf of somebody else, a written approval is generally needed).

* To provide a single invoice to business customers we would either need to receive multiple invoices from restaurants or generate ourselves invoices on their behalf. Also, if we talk about the intermediary model, we would need to either:

*Information shared in the discussion* ([related Slack thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02BXJSSPUL/p1653987914410929]):

* OPS team has issued a fine (200 EUR) for a stolen fuel card only once - it was a case where the police had stopped a Drive user who was under the influence and they also found 4 stolen fuel cards.
* We often don’t know if a user has taken a fuel card from the card - we typically hear about it from users who report a missing fuel card in the car they’re using.

*Decisions:*

* Let’s update the *Fuel card is missing* process in the KB article [User reported issues with fuelling or charging the car|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/internal/360021415640] to mention the related fine to encourage the user to return the fuel card (similar to how we have it in the missing car keys process):
** ask the user if they may have the fuel card
** ask to return it + provide instructions how
** if they refuse - then inform them about the fine
* No need to block the user, a mention of a fine and actually issuing the fine (if they don’t want to return the card) is fine.
* When it comes to repeat offenders (user profile comments show the user having taken fuel cards multiple times already), this is a signal of fuel card misuse - for which we already have the [Report of fuel card misuse or fuel theft|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/4795708281362--Reports-of-fuel-card-misuse-or-fuel-theft] process in place.

From a reclassification perspective, moving the billing from the couriers to Bolt can be problematic. While not any formal or explicit wording that would imply that this directly would lead to re classification, a lot of the regulatory / legislative discussions are focusing on empowering couriers to, for an example, build their own customer base. This could include preferred couriers choices as well as billing. We see this for an example in the latest wording from the presidency in the ongoing Plattform Work Directive negotiations; "_restriction of freedom, including through sanctions, to organise one’s work and control its execution”._ At the end of the day, platforms will have to accept that Couriers are entitled to a greater degree of influence over procedures. 

I am not sure if I can point to anything more concrete than this, but if we proceed we will have to be very cautious with wording, consent collection etc.

From previous experience with insurance companies:

→ They do insure items that do not have any registration marks (like construction and drilling equipment) - this falls under property insurance;

→ They do offer floating prices (mostly used with employees) - if we are in the given brackets, the price will stay the same. If we move to the next bracket, this can change the premium etc.

→ We don’t have any _Casco_ insurance on Bolt Drive vehicles - as the risk to benefit ratio for the companies went way up.

→ The premium is calculated on the data available to the insurance company - meaning that any processed claim will rise our monthly payments. Some claims would/should be handled in-house. This will rise operating costs.

Hi all

I had a call with our LT tax advisors just now. Their view is that, given that purchases can only be done through the app, the informational receipt we currently provide is sufficient for LT tax purposes. In particular, the info included on such informational receipts complies with the VAT invoicing requirements in Lithuania. 

In Lithuania, the tax authorities take a substance over form approach, and as such, even though we call the document an informational receipt, in substance it corresponds to an invoice. Going forward, if it is possible to issue actual invoices, better, but the tax advisors view was that it shouldn’t generally be a show stopper. 

My understanding is that there is no substantial difference between the info provided on the informational receipt and the numbers used for Lithuanian VAT compliance taken from the admin, so there should be no under reported/paid VAT in Lithuania. [~accountid:623c7881562ab90069f8f044] 

I also confirmed that the above conclusion does not change due to the fact that we have card readers in the shop (that I understand are not used in practice).
