Hi [~accountid:60e96a31131bf80069e1459f] As discussed, I had instructed DLA to look into this.

+*Here is my email to DLA (25 March):*+

Nuno (cc'd) and the Ride Hailing team in PT are envisaging trying a pilot with an existing Fleet Owner (FO), where the FO would employ as Full Time Employees (FTE) the drivers (which are usually independent). This wouldn't change the way our App works, and I don't really foresee any direct impact on us - however this would obviously have a direct impact on the FOs. 

I understand that there is in fact a high probability that, after the presumption of employment law is passed, we might be moving to this model for the whole supply market. 

Following Nuno's discussions with that FO, the below questions/comments were raised by the FO Legal Team - and even though these topics are more of a concern for the FO, we'd like to understand better how it works under PT law, more particularly if we want to try to do a pilot with that FO. I'd therefore be grateful for your views on the below please:

* "_It's not possible to fire a driver (who is employed as an FTE) who is suspended/blocked by a platform (e.g. Bolt), even if the suspension/block is due to malpractice and/or misconduct_" --> As you might remember, clause 4.8 of our T&Cs allow us to "immediately suspend the Taxi Operator’s and/or its Drivers’ access to the App Bolt, Bolt Accounts and Bolt Services during the investigation period if Bolt suspects there is a violation of these Terms and Conditions or fraudulent activity." So the question here is, if the driver is suspended by Bolt, the FO still has to employ him/her and cannot fire him/her?
* "I_t's illegal to suspend the salary payment of a driver while he/she is temporarily blocked by a platform_" --> Same situation as above, but the question is, if the driver is suspended, does the FO still have to pay him/her or do they have sufficient grounds to suspend his/her salary?
* "_Even if a driver only works 3 days per week (part time driver/worker), every time he/she does more than 8 hours per day (the max daily allowed working period), the additional hours need to be paid as overtime (with a different coefficient)_" --> Is this correct?
* As mentioned above, I don't really foresee any direct impact on us with such an employment model between the FO and the driver. I would say that it might even be better for us, in the sense that the driver would be directly employed by the FO and therefore we shouldn't face any risk of requalification request (as we do in France for instance, where the drivers who are not employed by the FO sometimes try to sue us - if we block them for instance, for bad behaviour - to obtain the requalification of their relationship with us as employee/employer ('requalification en contrat de travail') and therefore try to obtain all indemnities related to unfair dismissal, extra hours, etc). But keen to get your views on this as well, from a Bolt's perspective.

We need to have a legal assessment to understand if these comments have any legal basis or not - as we need to understand if the model described above would work for Bolt but also for the FOs.



+*Here is DLA response (31 May):*+

Please find below our comments on the queries raised.

+*A -*+ +"++_It's not possible to fire a driver (who is employed as an FTE) who is suspended/blocked by a platform (e.g. Bolt), even if the suspension/block is due to malpractice and/or misconduct_++" --> As you might remember, clause 4.8 of our T&Cs allow us to "immediately suspend the Taxi Operator’s and/or its Drivers’ access to the App Bolt, Bolt Accounts and Bolt Services during the investigation period if Bolt suspects there is a violation of these Terms and Conditions or fraudulent activity." So the question here is, if the driver is suspended by Bolt, the FO still has to employ him/her and cannot fire him/her?+

*DLA:* Yes. PT law does not allow for termination with notice or dismissal based on performance.

Employment contracts can terminate due to:

# Expiry (end of term contracts, retirement);
# Mutual agreement: required a written document signed by both parties; the parties are free to agree on the terms of the termination, including in respect to the amount of any severance;
# Disciplinary dismissal by the employer with just cause (based on a serious breach of the employee’s duties which leads to practical impossibility to maintain the employment relationship);
# Dismissal by the employer due to unsuitability of the employee to perform the job (very difficult to meet all legal requirements);
# Dismissal by the employer based on objective grounds (redundancy reasons), such as the need to down-sizing;
# Dismissal by the employee with notice (in case of permanent contract notice period is 30 or 60 days, depending on whether the employment contract was in force for up to 2 years or for a longer period);
# Constructive dismissal by the employee, with just cause.

Disciplinary dismissal by the employer, dismissal by the employer due to unsuitability, dismissal by the employer based on objective grounds and constructive dismissal by the employee, with just cause, require compliance with a previous legal procedure, according to mandatory law.

Therefore, even if the employee is suspended by a platform, FO still has to employ him/her unless one of the causes for termination mentioned above occurs.

+*B -*+ +"I++_t's illegal to suspend the salary payment of a driver while he/she is temporarily blocked by a platform_++" --> Same situation as above, but the question is, if the driver is suspended, does the FO still have to pay him/her or do they have sufficient grounds to suspend his/her salary?+

*DLA:* As a rule, payment of salary shall continue, even if the employee is suspended (e.g., in the scope of a disciplinary procedure). If the employee is blocked by a platform, the FO shall maintain the payment of salary.

+*C -*+ +"++_Even if a driver only works 3 days per week (part time driver/worker), every time he/she does more than 8 hours per day (the max daily allowed working period), the additional hours need to be paid as overtime (with a different coefficient)_++" --> Is this correct?+

*DLA:* Not necessarily.

Employees may be hired under flexible working schedules which allow for the performance of more than 8 hours of work per day – e.g., under a concentrated schedule, daily working period may be increased up to four hours per day, to concentrate the normal weekly working period into a maximum of four working days.

In any case, legal rules on the organization of the working time of mobile employees shall be complied with – e.g., the weekly duration of the working time of mobile employees, including overtime, shall not exceed 60 hours, and 48 on average, in a four-months reference period; also, the duration of work, including overtime, in case it covers the period between 0 and 5 am, may not exceed 10 hours per day.

+*E -*+ +As mentioned above, I don't really foresee any direct impact on us with such an employment model between the FO and the driver. I would say that it might even be better for us, in the sense that the driver would be directly employed by the FO and therefore we shouldn't face any risk of requalification request (as we do in France for instance, where the drivers who are not employed by the FO sometimes try to sue us - if we block them for instance, for bad behaviour - to obtain the requalification of their relationship with us as employee/employer ('requalification en contrat de travail') and therefore try to obtain all indemnities related to unfair dismissal, extra hours, etc). But keen to get your views on this as well, from a Bolt's perspective.+

*DLA:* We believe your assessment is correct. However, if FO qualifies these drivers as employees and controls their activity as other FO and/or Bolt directly, other drivers may resort to this qualification to compare themselves and sue FO and/or Bolt for requalification.

Hi [~accountid:5cd9daa0bc70090d6ce26227] and team - please see the updated draft and I welcome your thoughts on some of the points, which are related to the below. Also important context: 

*I.*                 +*Overview*+:

* As we understand, the purpose of the agreement is to have the Fleet providing workforce to Bolt Stores in the form of *outsourcing.*
* Under Polish law, there is a specific regulation concerning temporary employment (Polish: _praca tymczasowa_) which, *if applicable, would impose several obligations in terms of employment on both Bolt and the Fleet.*
* As a result of the above, it is important to draw up an agreement so there are arguments to consider the agreement with the Fleet as an outsourcing agreement rather than as a temporary employment agreement. The proposed changes were aimed to emphasise that Bolt uses services of a Fleet (rather than its employees) and that the Fleet manages employees and bears liability for their performance and fulfilment of services.
* However, taking into the account the scope of services, *we cannot exclude a risk that in case of a control by the authorities*, after verification of actual scope of services provided by the Fleet/Fleet’s Employees, *the agreement will be considered as temporary employment agreement.*
* It is recommended to analyse how the Services will be fulfilled in day-to-day operations and by whom. If Bolt uses at the same time all available options to deliver goods to its clients e.g.: (i) own personnel; (ii) temporary workers provided by job agency; (iii) outsourcing providers; such model may be difficult to explain to Polish ZUS (Social Insurance Authority) and Polish Labour Inspectorate.  

*II.*               +*Outsourcing vs temporary employment*+

* *Applicable law*

+Outsourcing+ is governed by the Civil Code and freedom of contract where the content of an agreement is generally agreed between parties.

+Temporary employment+ is governed by special act on temporary employment which *imposes numerous obligations on both agency (the Fleet) and employer-user (Bolt).*

* *Eligibility to do business activity*

+Outsourcing+ is not a regulated business activity (any company may be a party to such agreement without obtaining additional consents, certificates etc.).

+Temporary employment+ is a *regulated business activity and requires prior registration as a temporary employment agency*. *Lack of such registration will likely cause imposition of penalties on the agency.*

* *Management of employees*

+Outsourcing:+ Employees are under the management of the employer (Fleet) and an entity for whom the services are performed (Bolt) cannot manage those employees. 

+Temporary employment:+ Employees are under the management of the employer-user (Bolt).

* *Obligations*

+Outsourcing+: generally, obligations are stipulated in the agreement and agreed between parties pursuant to freedom of contract.

+Temporary employment+: obligations of the agency or employer-user are strictly governed by the act on temporary employment (e.g. content of the mandatory agreement between the agency and employer-user, right to holidays of employees, max. amount of temporary work etc.).

* *Liability*

+Outsourcing:+ outsourcing company (Fleet) bears full liability for providing the services up to the total amount of damages.

+Temporary employment:+ Employee bears limited liability as stipulated in the temporary employment act and Employment Code.

*III.*              +*Consequences of qualifying the agreement as temporary employment agreement*+

* In case of a control by the authorities, the most analysed factor (in defining an actual agreement concluded) is the factual management of the employees and whether the service is performed by the external company who specialised in such area and not in a field of delivering workforce to companies in need. The later is a classic temporary job agency business.
* Qualification of the agreement as temporary agency agreement may lead to imposition of penalties, obligation to pay or return VAT and to pay social security contributions for the employees*.*

{code:sql}WITH stop_jitters AS (
  SELECT MIN(timestamp_ms) AS ts_start, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS ts_end, vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng, ST_Point(lng, lat) AS pt
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      SUM(igition_switch) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ignition_id
    FROM (
      SELECT *, 
        COALESCE((
          (ignition != LAG(ignition) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms)) OR
          (order_id != LAG(order_id) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms))
        )::integer, 1) AS igition_switch
      FROM (
        SELECT timestamp_ms, entity_id AS vehicle_id, order_id, 
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'is_ignition_on') AS ignition,
               lat, lng,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_pdop')::decimal AS gnss_pdop,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_hdop')::decimal AS gnss_hdop
        FROM ext_tracking_live.tracking_car_sharing_locations
        WHERE created_at_date>'2022-05-01' AND JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_status')='fix'
          -- AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(lng,lat), ST_Point(24.745293, 59.437339)) < 15000 -- FILTER OUT FERRIES (hopefully), only 15km around Raekoja
          -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-14' AND order_id=3621305 -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
          -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-24' --AND vehicle_id IN (1974,1254,777,1485,735,495,2013) -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
      )
    )
  )
  WHERE ignition='false'
  GROUP BY vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
),



stop_centroids AS (
  SELECT l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id,
    ST_AsEWKT(ST_Centroid(ST_Collect(l.pt)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY l.lat,l.lng)) AS centroid
  FROM stop_jitters AS l
  WHERE l.gnss_pdop = 0 AND l.gnss_hdop = 0
  GROUP BY l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id
)


SELECT gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop,
  -- MAX(accuracy_m) AS accuracy_m, 
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p95,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.97) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p97,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.995) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p995,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p999,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p9999,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99999) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY accuracy_m) AS accuracy_p99999,
  COUNT(1) AS hits
FROM (
  SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, 
    MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, ST_GeomFromEWKT(centroid))) AS accuracy_m,  
    AVG(ST_DistanceSphere(j.pt, ST_GeomFromEWKT(centroid))) AS accuracy_avg_m,
    COUNT(1) AS hits, centroid, MIN(j.ts_start) AS ts
  FROM stop_jitters AS j
  JOIN stop_centroids AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id) -- SKIPPING ignition_ids only with poor accuracy
  GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, centroid
  HAVING accuracy_m < 1000
)
GROUP BY gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop
ORDER BY 1,2 -- j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop
LIMIT 300 {code}

After discussing with data scientist, the sample size for the test should be X per group, not X divided by 3. So if we want to have 80% confidence level and margin of error at 5%, the sample size for each group is ~150, totaling to ~300. 5% margin of error means the change between group must be greater than 5% to ensure statistical validity. If the actual change is smaller, then the sample size must also be bigger (for example, if the actual difference only 1%, then we need more sample. *What do we know so far?*

* It’s not an RxJS issue based on extensive debugging of the {{network-service}} library.
* It’s not an issue with the HTTP client we use - based on the fact that the same client is used for polling (polling remains functional after connection restoration).
* It’s probably not an issue with underlying {{whatwg-fetch}} or RN {{XMLHttpRequest}}, based on the fact that those are also used for polling, which remains functional.
* Presence of bug depends on the host used by {{network-service}}. {{boltsvc}} is fine, for example (explains why polling remains functional).
* The requests never reach the server based on replacing the connection check host with a custom server exposed via {{ngrok}}.
* Since {{Settings > Close app}} clears the issue on an emu, it must have something to do with the “process” the app is running in.
* Since no issues could be detected down to the {{RCTNetworking}} layer, it’s probably not an issue with the JS libs we use. Need to debug the Java layer.
* The endpoint remains accessible via the device’s shell.

Our policy for video surveillance can be found on Confluence[ here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3489661435/Policy+on+using+video+surveillance+on+the+premises+of+Bolt]. 

The steps to reach compliance with the cameras installed are the following:

# *Legal basis and purpose of the video surveillance:*
The legal basis for processing data through CCTV is legitimate interest. Legitimate interest requires at first step that the purposes of using cameras are identified (this is asked in the questionnaire). 
# *Positioning the cameras*
The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is +not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms+ etc. 
The positioning of the video cameras should be aimed to record areas which correspond to possible threat (theft, property damage). 
# *Retention time*
Under Croatian law this is max 6 months but my advice is to limit the retention time to what is strictly necessary. I.e. time needed to detect possible thefts/damages/unauthorised access. E.g. retention period of 72 hours seems appropriate, since it can be assumed that any damage to the facade, such as graffiti or theft is recognizable and an export to can be carried out).

After the retention period set the footage must be deleted automatically.  
# *Access control and logs*
Access rules must be put in place on who has access to the footage and every access to footage is logged. 
# *Transparency and information requirement*
Information/warning signs should be installed with the following information:

-Information that there is video surveillance in the area (e.g camera picture, “We have video surveillance”)
-Controller (“Controller information”)
-Legal basis: Legitimate interest
-Information of where further information can be found (QR code or link to the [global privacy notice on video surveillance|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance]). 

We also have a template sign which can be made to stickers. However I need to change the controller information to Bolt Services HR d.o.o in the file. Will find someone who can help me with that 🙂 
# *Data protection agreement with service provider*
If we use third party service providers (for hosting etc) then a DPA must be signed with them. [~accountid:62275121c88f10006831a6f6] or [~accountid:6163fba57a6be400714cbb51] - let me know if we have a service provider for cameras and what is their role or where do we store the data?

Hi, just wanted to capture in this ticket also the external counsel advice and some of the discussion we have had over email. From Andrei G (my addition in bold):

_There are several topics which need to be considered in relation to this type of campaign, as follows:_

_(i) this is not a consumer oriented campaign, but rather a campaign aimed at providing an incentive for partners' (i.e. fleets) employees to focus their efforts on Bolt. For this reason, it is necessary to obtain the_ *_fleet's consent before offering this type of campaign_* _to their employees._ *_There is judicial practice in Romania where this type of incentive offered to the employees of a partner without the approval of the employer was deemed as bribery_*_. The rationale behind this is that the end goal of the incentive may conflict with the fleet's commercial interest (e.g. the fleet's commercial strategy may be to focus their efforts on another platform), and this direct relation with their employees bypasses the employer. To this end, we have included a condition for participation that the courier is either self employed or has the approval of the fleet to enter the contest. For the same reason, it would be advisable from a practical perspective to have an opt-in step, rather than automatically entering all couriers into the contest._

_(ii) from a competition perspective, Bolt should check if it may be deemed to hold a dominant position in either Bucharest or Cluj (a 40% market share is an indicator for dominance). Incentives applied by dominant undertakings have been found abusive when given in exchange for customer loyalty or when they are found to be loyalty-inducing. For instance, incentives which are likely to induce exclusivity (i.e. if in order to achieve the 30 orders/week entering condition, the courier would need to source over 80% of his/hers orders from the Bolt Platform) are likely to be considered an abuse of dominant position, if Bolt were to hold such position (see Case T-286/09 Intel v Commission ECLI:EU:T:2014:54)._

It was discussed that since Bolt does not have a 40% market share - the second point can be disregarded. 

With regard to the first point, [~accountid:5eea2a7d2b9c4c0abfee86c1] has confirmed that, like with other weekly campaigns, the prize in this case will be paid to the courier via the fleet - and Andrei G commented that with the bonus passing through the fleet, “which means that if they are willing to pass it on, it should be equivalent to them accepting this commercial arrangement”. Andrei G also stated “there is probably a great degree of implied agreement from fleet owners because obviously these promotions benefit all parties involved“. 

A separate point is to consider amending the courier T&Cs going forward so that they will automatically deem consent to such campaigns - [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] to raise this with product counsel (Julia and Marilin) to see how to best to achieve this.

Hey [~accountid:5eaa92cbe3c0900b9328085a], thanks a lot for your response.

*All in all, short response to your question is yes, we are required to explain to the couriers why they are suspended or terminated.* Longer explanation may be found below.

Under EU law, we are required to explain to the courier the reasons for suspending and/or terminating him/her. Please find our action points in case of suspension and termination below:

* *Suspension.* If we are suspending the courier from the platform, we are required to provide him with reasons for suspension prior to or at the time of the suspension taking effect. The reasons are required to be provided in a form which is reproducible (email, letter, chat communication that is possible to store somewhere etc). Afterwards, the courier should be given opportunity to explain why he/she behaved in a certain way. After the receipt of such explanation, we should carefully assess whether there are indeed any reasons for suspension. If there are are reasons for suspension, we are required to suspend the courier. If there are no reasons for suspension, we are not required to suspend the courier. 
* *Termination*. If we want to terminate the couriers, we are required to provide reasons for that to the courier at least 30 days prior to their termination taking effect. The reasons are required to be provided in a form which is reproducible (email, letter, chat communication that is possible to store somewhere etc). Afterwards, the courier should be given opportunity to explain why he/she behaved in a certain way. After the receipt of such explanation, we should carefully assess whether there are indeed any reasons for termination. If there are are reasons for termination, we are required to terminate the courier. If there are no reasons for termination, we are not required to terminate the courier. 
** The notice period of 30 days shall not apply in the following cases:
*** we as a platform are subject to a legal or regulatory obligation which requires us to terminate the provision of the whole of our online intermediation services to a courier in a manner which does not allow us to respect that notice period; or
*** we terminate the courier under an imperative reason pursuant to national law;
*** we can demonstrate that the courier concerned has repeatedly infringed our terms and conditions, resulting in the termination of the provision of the whole of the online intermediation services in question.

Hi.

yes - the general direction of travel contractually is “leave doors open” with catch-all provisions, even in cases we aim to be more granular (like spelling out product-specific cases when actions can be taken). Looking at T&C terms it is clear that this case on hand is caught by art 13.3 and we can point to it. BUT if the claim goes further the assessment courts would do is whether our T&Cs pass the P2B bar and are aligned? if not - the clause (and termination) will be deemed void and null. Leaving us to fall back on general contract clauses under applicable law.

In case of drivers we need to run an assessment if this would hold in court vis-a-vis what P2B is saying:

P2B art 4 says that a rule of thumb when terminating Drivers access to a platform is that we need to notify him 30 days in advance giving reasons.

So our current T&Cs art 13.2 is clearly too broad in eyes of P2B in general 😞 

However, the way we think about HP cases (harassment / fraud  or anything else that potentially amounts to “breach of law”) is that we take action immediately signalling it as “suspension without prior notice” (P2B does not prohibit this). Then when HP case is processed and we are comfortable that facts are right the suspension becomes a termination converts into termination. Our approach is that P2B art 4(4) also does not prohibit to terminate without any additional process or notice in cases of breach of laws/regulations; serious breaches of our T&Cs or other repeated breaches of our T&Cs. The test under P2B if we can terminate Driver immediately is in general “wherther local laws do allows immediate contract termination” which in cases of breaches of law (let alone criminal activity) is usually the case.

So art 13.3 of our T&Cs is basically attempting to lay out and specify these cases which are allowed under the P2B:

* breach of law / regulation
* serious T&C breaches: disparage of Bolt, harm to Brand, reputation. 

Now in this particular case of bringing a police note saying that investigation is closed, the essential legal questions are:

* can we still qualify suspected activity as breach of law if law enforcement agency is stating that  they did not qualify it as such given evidence? OR
* can we claim that suspected activity the way we documented it amounts to serious breach of our T&Cs / disparagement of Bolt and harm to reputation PLUS can this  effectively pass P2B test in art 4(4).

Since PL Driver T&Cs are governed by PL law, it would be a reasonable exercise to double check with local counsel on:

* Does the PL contract law allow for an immediate termination in cases of suspected criminal activity when law enforcement has not opened the case and no criminal proceedings have been initiated? OR would such situation and our termination pass a P2B test in art 4(4) under PL law? 

And outside the pure legal arguments - the stance should still be:

* in cases of HP incidents: immediate suspension
* normally suspension to translate into termination, unless our investigation shows there is no reason for this
* In case of doubt could fall back on a 2 strike policy: if similar reports reach us again, terminate immediately based on “repeated breach of our T&Cs” (either reputation / brand damage or any other broad safety clauses).

in connection with the unlawful provision of discounts, it is possible to commit in particular and most often the following offenses. However, state supervision will always assess the individual characteristics of the case and it will always depend on the specific circumstances according to which it will be assessed whether the specific offense was committed or not.

* *breach of the obligation of honesty in the sale of products (Section 3 of Act No. 634/1992 Coll., on consumer protection)*

These are mainly cases where traders incorrectly charge the declared price of goods, when, for example, the price stated for the goods in the mobile application is different from the price charged in reality. A fine of up to CZK 5 000 000 can be imposed for violating this obligation.

* *breach of the seller's obligation to inform consumers in accordance with price regulations (Section 12 of Act No. 634/1992 Coll., on Consumer Protection)*

These are, for example, cases where the consumer was not informed with the final price valid at the time of the offer, or this price was stated in an unclear or incomplete manner, e.g. the price was given before the discount and the information about the discount was given only as a percentage without the final price. Or more price information was provided on the discounted goods and the consumer was thus unable to determine which of those prices was valid. A fine of up to CZK 5 000 000 can be imposed for violating this obligation.

* *breach of the obligation regarding marking of goods with prices (§13 of Act No. 526/1990 Coll. on prices)*

These are cases where the goods are not properly marked so that the consumer has the opportunity to familiarize himself with the price before negotiating the purchase of goods. A fine of up to CZK 1 000 000 can be imposed for violating this obligation.

+*Further clarification received from OC, 19 May 2022:*+

Nous comprenons que _la mise à disposition de chauffeurs ayant le statut de travailleur indépendant concerne la majorité des gestionnaires de flottes_. Autrement dit, la plupart des gestionnaires de flottes avec lesquels Bolt envisagent de conclure des partenariats n’emploient pas les chauffeurs par le biais de contrats de travail mais par des contrats commerciaux.

Dans ce cadre, nous vous confirmons que :

* Le risque de requalification des contrats commerciaux (établis entre les gestionnaires de flotte et les chauffeurs) en contrats de travail est identique ;
* Le risque lié à la reconnaissance d’une situation de co-emploi entre Bolt, les gestionnaires de flottes et les chauffeurs n’est pas modifié. Si en travaillant sous le statut de salariés en vertu d’un contrat de travail conclu avec les gestionnaires de flottes, les chauffeurs seraient moins enclins à revendiquer l’existence d’un contrat de travail avec Bolt (et les gestionnaires de flottes) devant les juridictions prud’homales et pénales dans la mesure où ils bénéficieraient déjà des droits qui découlent de leur statut de salarié, *le fait qu’ils ne soient pas salariés des gestionnaires de flotte ne facilitera pas pour autant la qualification de co-emploi*. En effet, *une telle qualification est strictement encadré et la Cour de cassation impose une véritable immixtion du co-employeur (Bolt) dans la gestion de la relation contractuelle. Même si Bolt impose certaines conditions aux chauffeurs,* +*le risque de reconnaissance du co emploi paraît assez limité*+.

De plus, il convient de souligner qu’un arrêt récent de la Cour de cassation est particulièrement intéressant sur cette matière (_Cass. soc. 13 avril 2022_).

Dans cette affaire, un chauffeur avait conclu un contrat de location de longue durée d’un véhicule ainsi qu’un contrat d’adhésion au système informatisé de la société Voxtur (Le Cab). A la suite de la rupture des relations contractuelles, le chauffeur demande la requalification en contrat de travail.

La Cour d’appel avait requalifié la relation contractuelle en contrat de travail mais la Cour de cassation a décidé de casser cet arrêt. Certes la Cour de cassation a renvoyé cette affaire devant une autre formation de la Cour d’appel et il convient d’attendre cette décision mais il est intéressant de noter que la Cour de cassation refuse la requalification de la relation contractuelle en contrat de travail car la Cour d’appel _« en se déterminant ainsi, par des motifs insuffisants à caractériser l'exercice d'un travail au sein d'un service organisé selon des conditions déterminées unilatéralement par la société Voxtur, sans constater que celle-ci avait adressé à M. \[T] des directives sur les modalités d'exécution du travail, qu'elle disposait du pouvoir d'en contrôler le respect et d'en sanctionner l'inobservation »._

Ainsi, la Cour de cassation rappelle qu’il est impératif de caractériser un *lien de subordination incluant le contrôle de l’activité du chauffeur (par le recours à sa géolocalisation) et le pouvoir de sanction de l’employeur (à travers le système de notation)* pour qu’un contrat de travail soit reconnu.

Quelle que soit la nature de la relation contractuelle entre les gestionnaires de flotte et les chauffeurs, il conviendra de s’assurer que Bolt ne dispose pas d’un pouvoir de sanction direct sur les chauffeurs.

En tout état de cause, il conviendra de s’assurer que les gestionnaire de flottes demeure le principal interlocuteur des chauffeurs.

DLA have assessed the feasibility of the proposed deal in Portugal and have identified the following legal risks - {color:#ff5630}I’ve added in red some questions for you please{color} 😉 

*1.Regulatory risks*

*a) Platform operator*

* The TVDE legal regime does not allow for platform operators to own TVDE vehicles, nor to finance or be an interested party in the acquisition, renting or leasing of TVDE vehicles. The breach of this rule results in administrative offence liability. 
* The PT law defines the platform operator in a formalistic way, corresponding to the legal person that is licensed to provide the ride-hailing services.
* In Portugal, the entity that holds the license to operate as a platform is Bolt Portugal, so the above mentioned prohibition applies to – strictly speaking - Bolt Portugal.
* +The solution would therefore be to use an entity other than Bolt Portugal for the purposes of the co-financing.+ [~accountid:60e96a31131bf80069e1459f]{color:#ff5630} is it possible?{color}
* There is, of course, the risk that if another Bolt entity (other than Bolt Portugal) is used for this purpose, the connection be used to claim that it is Bolt Portugal indirectly. However, considering the formalistic approach enshrined in the law, we consider that there is a strong argument in favour of only considering the formal holder of the license in Portugal to be prevented from financing the acquisition of vehicles. +A possibility that would reduce the risk even further would be to use a partner with no corporate connection to Bolt+. Now they are contacting to remove person B’s licence and add their own 

4. person A verified their licence to person B’s account cuz person B didn’t have a licence on their hand and they were in a rush. Person A drove, forgot to remove their licence from person B’s account and now person B wants to verify their own licence to use the service as per our TnC



These should be our main reasons for contact in such cases. In all of those, the users typically try to verify their own licence after having a successful verification of someone else in their profile.

Hello Eliise\!

The Commerce team issues refunds from BB to the user’s payment method only in high priority cases.

It seems like this is not a one-time bug but a feature built into Bolt Balance. There are 2 problematic scenarios that I can think of at the moment:

* the fine could not be captured, went into user’s Bolt Balance as debt and was captured with the next ride. Refunding the fined trip will add the money to BB, refunding the next ride will send the money back to the user’s payment method (fee for the ride + the debt added to it). This way we can fulfil our promise but it usually happens after the first refund goes to BB so the user is left with ~50 EUR in the balance and we have to send a SD ticket to delete it.
* the fine could not be captured, went into user’s Bolt Balance as debt and the user topped-up their account to pay off the debt - in this case it looks like CS is unable to issue a refund to the user’s payment method.

Ideally we should be able to always issue a full refund to the user’s payment method if necessary. If not, agents should have clear guidelines on how to identify which scenario they’re dealing with in order to provide the user with accurate info.

Thank you\!

{code:sql}WITH stop_jitters AS (
  SELECT MIN(timestamp_ms) AS ts_start, MAX(timestamp_ms) AS ts_end, vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng, ST_Point(lng, lat) AS pt
  FROM (
    SELECT *,
      SUM(igition_switch) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS ignition_id
    FROM (
      SELECT *, 
        COALESCE((
          (ignition != LAG(ignition) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms)) OR
          (order_id != LAG(order_id) OVER (ORDER BY vehicle_id, order_id, timestamp_ms))
        )::integer, 1) AS igition_switch
      FROM (
        SELECT timestamp_ms, entity_id AS vehicle_id, order_id, 
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'is_ignition_on') AS ignition,
               lat, lng,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_pdop')::decimal AS gnss_pdop,
               JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_hdop')::decimal AS gnss_hdop
        FROM ext_tracking_live.tracking_car_sharing_locations
        WHERE created_at_date>'2022-05-01' AND JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(vehicle_metadata, 'gnss_status')='fix' AND order_id!=0
          -- AND ST_DistanceSphere(ST_Point(lng,lat), ST_Point(24.745293, 59.437339)) < 15000 -- FILTER OUT FERRIES (hopefully), only 15km around Raekoja
          -- AND created_at_date='2022-05-14' AND order_id=3621305 -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
          AND created_at_date='2022-05-24' -- AND vehicle_id IN (1974,1254,777,1485,735,495,2013) -- EXTRA LIMIT TO REMOVE
      )
    )
  )
  WHERE ignition='false'
  GROUP BY vehicle_id, order_id, ignition_id, gnss_pdop, gnss_hdop, lat, lng
),



stop_centroids AS (
  SELECT l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id,
    ST_AsEWKT(ST_Centroid(ST_Collect(l.pt)) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY l.lat,l.lng)) AS centroid,
    ST_Area(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS area_m2,
    ST_Perimeter(ST_ConvexHull(ST_Collect(l.pt))::geography) AS perimeter_m
  FROM stop_jitters AS l
  WHERE l.gnss_pdop = 0 AND l.gnss_hdop = 0
  GROUP BY l.vehicle_id, l.order_id, l.ignition_id
)


SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id,

  ANY_VALUE(area_m2) AS area_m2,
  ANY_VALUE(perimeter_m) AS perimeter_m,
  COALESCE(ANY_VALUE(area_m2) / NULLIF(ANY_VALUE(perimeter_m), 0), 0) AS area_to_perimeter_m
FROM stop_jitters AS j
JOIN stop_centroids AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id)
GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id
ORDER BY accuracy_m DESC

Hey [~accountid:5eaa92cbe3c0900b9328085a], thank you for approaching us. In legal terms, if we are substituting the assigned courier with another courier, then:

* we are terminating the agency agreement with one courier and concluding a new one with the new courier, and 
* the client is terminating the delivery agreement with an existing courier and concluding a delivery agreement with a new courier. 

The first challenge I see here is that we have no right to terminate the agreement with the courier under these circumstances, except for the cases where the courier has repeatedly violated our Courier T&Cs. However, I would say that this can be possibly overcome if we obtain an express consent from the courier to assign his/her delivery to another courier. Please note that the substitute should be onboarded to our Bolt Food Platform when he/she receives the delivery assignment.

The second challenge I see here is that we will be terminating client’s agreement with the courier on client’s behalf. I believe that for this we need to ask for client’s express consent as well, by asking in-app something like: _“The courier assigned to your order is unfortunately unable to deliver your order. Would you like us to ask another courier to deliver your order?”_ As noted by yourself, the substitution may only happen before the courier has picked up the order.

Another challenge I see here is how shall we distribute the earnings before the courier who got into an accident, and the substitute of that courier. Have it been thought through?



Br,

Julia

So regarding why in the contract the rent amount is 16 EUR/m2:

As the terms of the agreement stipulate that if our investment of 300 EUR / m2 in the finishing of your premises is not enough, then as the Lessee we have 3 scenarios:

#  To reduce office fit-out price requirements
# To invest any costs for the fit-out that top 300 EUR/m2 ourselves.
# To agree with the Lessor that we have a higher rent price (in this case 16 EUR / m2) but do not pay anything extra for the fit-out.

Hey Piotr\! Sorry for the late response, gathering narrative took a while :)

Regarding points 1 and 2:

* Since around Q3 of 2021, we have been noticing issues with Phone call CSAT. After escalating the problem to CS Product team, we were informed that indeed, there was an issue with Phone CSAT surveys, and that this would not be fixed until the transition to Beehive. This in effect meant, that we receive close to zero phone CSAT surveys (especially compared to ticket surveys) and the few we do get back, have almost always been rated positive and our CSAT for phone remained at nearly exactly 100% for months. Thus, we have not been investigating phone CSAT much since the problem arose. However, recently we have begun to intensify our efforts in assessing phone call quality, especially through the work of our ES. As a result, we have found that the quality is a lot worse than the CSAT would suggest - the results in full can be found on the ES decks.
* So, to answer your points directly - measuring impact on CSAT is not possible, as we have ceased to measure CSAT on phone support completely. Instead, we rely on manual quality checks. As for the second point - this isn’t a ‘drastic change’ per se. We only started to check phone call quality relatively not long ago. Previously, phone call quality was mostly unknown to us. So these quality issues could have been ongoing for a long time, but we are only aware of this now. While there are some differences between sites for Majorel, we are finding that some quality issues were common for all sites at once and not isolated to any teams.

Regarding point 3:

* Yes, feedback regarding these findings has been passed on to MA management and SCs repeatedly, especially during our weekly quality syncs, but also stressed during out WBRs and MBRs. While this has brought some results - for example, issues with agents missing the verification questions during phone calls have subsided slightly - some issues persist and there is no 100% elimination of problems. Improvement has been relatively slow thus far, especially when it comes to agent tone and empathy. I will be sure to pass on the info and the feedback to the listed persons, but it is also quite evident, that even despite our close work with those people, the progress is not as rapid as we would hope it to be.

As for 4:

* Yes, there are some select positive outliers, for example these two agents, one from GGN and one from NBO:
** [https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/users/381359367560/assigned_tickets|https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/users/381359367560/assigned_tickets]
** [https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/users/382870548039/assigned_tickets|https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/users/382870548039/assigned_tickets]
* However, the overall level of quality remains significantly below our expectations and suggests a systemic issue with the entirety of the teams, rather than just an issue with some of the agents. Majorel also did not pay attention to the phone call quality until our ES begun their quality assessments, and did not provide adequate feedback after after the first few rounds of our analysis and providing narrative to the teams.

Please let me know if I should fill in with any other info and hope it will be useful feedback\!

Cheers\!

FROM (
  SELECT j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, 
    ROUND(MAX(ST_DistanceSphere(jlo.pt, ST_GeomFromEWKT(centroid)))*100)/100 AS worst_accuracy_m
    -- ANY_VALUE(a.accuracy_m) AS dillution_0_accuracy_m
  FROM stop_jitters AS j
  JOIN stop_jitters AS jlo ON (j.vehicle_id = jlo.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = jlo.order_id AND j.ignition_id = jlo.ignition_id AND j.gnss_pdop >= jlo.gnss_pdop AND j.gnss_hdop >= jlo.gnss_hdop)
  JOIN stop_centroids AS c ON (j.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = c.order_id AND j.ignition_id = c.ignition_id) -- SKIPPING ignition_ids without the 0,0 accuracy
  JOIN stop_accuracy AS a ON (j.vehicle_id = a.vehicle_id AND j.order_id = a.order_id AND j.ignition_id = a.ignition_id) -- AND filtering out the towing
  GROUP BY j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop, centroid
  HAVING worst_accuracy_m < 1000
)
GROUP BY gnss_hdop, gnss_pdop
HAVING COUNT(1) > 9
ORDER BY 1,2 -- j.vehicle_id, j.order_id, j.ignition_id, j.gnss_pdop, j.gnss_hdop
LIMIT 300{noformat}
